title: `BIGINT % BIGINT`
description: `MIN % -1` raises `Overflow in division` (duckdb-R3); the SQL writes that case out.

Round 4 (probes): at TINYINT and SMALLINT `%` keeps the type and truncates (`-7 % 3 = -1`, `7 % -3 = 1`, `MIN % 1 = 0`), and `MIN % -1` raises `Out of Range Error: Overflow in division of MIN / -1` at all four widths, from table columns.
The docs are silent on the sign of `%` and on `MIN % -1`: a docs gap. No upstream test pins `MIN % -1` below HUGEINT; it may change between versions.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe` runs the function at each signature on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the 64-bit bounds, 0.5, ±2.5, 1e308, ±inf, NaN, NULL), one row at a time from columns, under every combination of `error_on_division_by_zero` and `ieee_floating_point_ops`. Lean evaluates the Substrait call on the same rows once per candidate value of its option (`substrait-check --outcomes`), and the candidates whose outcomes all match are DuckDB's options. No input is -0.0 (duckdb-R14).

evidence.note: ModuloOperator: left % right, C++'s truncating remainder
BinaryNumericDivideWrapper: MIN and -1 raise `Overflow in division` before OP runs; a zero divisor raises or gives NULL

provenance.notes: `%` shares `//`'s wrapper, one template instantiated per width, so `MIN % -1` raises at i8, i16 and i32 as at i64, and the remainder truncates (C++ `%`, the dividend's sign). `MIN % -1` is also the only overflow of `%`: every other remainder fits.

evidence.note: `-90 % 20, 90 % -20, -90 % -20` → -10, 10, -10 on INTEGER literals (and on HUGEINT): the remainder truncates and takes the dividend's sign (i32)
`HUGEINT MIN % -1` raises `Out of Range Error`; HUGEINT only

provenance.notes: No test takes a remainder of a negative TINYINT, SMALLINT or BIGINT, or `MIN % -1` at i8 … i64, so `division_type` at i8 and i16, and `min_mod_neg_one` and `overflow` at i8 … i32, stay at the source reading (i64 at the probe). The HUGEINT test raises as the shared wrapper does.

provenance.checked_by: characterization pipeline round 4 (probes; duckdb 2.0.0, Python, macOS arm64)
provenance.notes: `python -m sverify_dev.probe --observations --write` runs each query on a fresh connection under `TimeZone = 'UTC'` (or its own setup) and records the rows or the error as they come; `tests/test_probe.py::test_observations_are_current` checks they are current.

evidence.note: % 'Modulo (remainder)'; zero divisor raises; silent on the sign and on MIN % -1
